question: outcome-supervised and pre-fetch routing; counterfactual utility labels from paired rollouts; cost-aware gating; published evidence that deciding to retrieve before the fetch preserves quality

sources.citation: Soyeong Jeong, Jinheon Baek, Sukmin Cho, Sung Ju Hwang, Jong C. Park. Adaptive-RAG: Learning to Adapt Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models through Question Complexity. NAACL 2024. arXiv:2403.14403v2.
claims: A smaller LM classifier selects the retrieval strategy, including no-retrieval, before the strategy runs.
The classifier's labels are collected from the actual predicted outcomes of the candidate models, not from a fixed heuristic.
The paper reports improved overall efficiency and accuracy against adaptive-retrieval baselines.
sources.how_verified: abstract and submission metadata read on 2026-11-17 from https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.14403
sources.relevance: direct precedent for an outcome-supervised router whose decision precedes retrieval; the S52 router differs in deciding per token from the causal hidden state rather than per query from a complexity class

sources.citation: Akari Asai, Zeqiu Wu, Yizhong Wang, Avirup Sil, Hannaneh Hajishirzi. Self-RAG: Learning to Retrieve, Generate, and Critique through Self-Reflection. arXiv:2310.11511v1.
claims: Indiscriminate retrieval regardless of necessity can reduce versatility or produce unhelpful responses.
Self-RAG trains one LM to adaptively retrieve on demand using reflection tokens, and it can decide not to retrieve.
It reports gains over retrieval-augmented Llama2-chat and ChatGPT on open-domain QA, reasoning and fact verification.
sources.how_verified: abstract and submission metadata read on 2026-11-17 from https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.11511
sources.relevance: the retrieve-on-demand premise; Self-RAG's reflection token is a decoded decision, whereas S52 predicts utility from a causal hidden state before the read

sources.citation: Zhengbao Jiang, Frank F. Xu, Luyu Gao, Zhiqing Sun, Qian Liu, Jane Dwivedi-Yu, Yiming Yang, Jamie Callan, Graham Neubig. Active Retrieval Augmented Generation. EMNLP 2023. arXiv:2305.06983v2.
claims: Methods that actively decide when and what to retrieve across generation are a generalization of retrieve-once RAG.
FLARE retrieves and regenerates only when a predicted upcoming sentence contains low-confidence tokens.
FLARE is superior or competitive on four long-form knowledge-intensive generation tasks.
sources.relevance: a low-confidence trigger is a pre-fetch signal, but it is an absolute confidence, not an estimate of the marginal utility of the read; S52's label is the paired difference

sources.citation: Weihang Su, Yichen Tang, Qingyao Ai, Zhijing Wu, Yiqun Liu. DRAGIN: Dynamic Retrieval Augmented Generation based on the Information Needs of Large Language Models. arXiv:2403.10081v3.
claims: Dynamic RAG must decide when to retrieve during generation; static rules are identified as a weakness.
DRAGIN decides from the LM's real-time information need and reports superior results on four knowledge-intensive datasets.
sources.how_verified: abstract and submission metadata read on 2026-11-17 from https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.10081
sources.relevance: supports per-generation-step decisions; DRAGIN scores a query/uncertainty signal, not a counterfactual outcome difference

sources.topic: counterfactual utility labels from paired rollouts
sources.citation: Wenhao Zou, Xianglong Liu, Wendong Bi, Hanjie Wang, Simin Zhao, Gong Zhi. CoBRA: Learning Tool-Use Boundaries via Counterfactual Margins. EMNLP 2026. arXiv:2609.00967v1.
claims: Triggers based on absolute difficulty, confidence or final reward lack an explicit estimate of the instance-level marginal benefit of tool use.
CoBRA builds internal and external experts from the same base model and collects paired trajectories, estimating the reward margin between answering with and without tools.
The margin partitions data into internal-favored, external-favored and ambiguous cases and supervises the boundary decision.
Retrieval is the main tool; the experiments report improved tool-use efficiency and boundary-sensitive answer accuracy.
sources.how_verified: abstract and submission metadata read on 2026-11-17 from https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.00967
sources.relevance: closest published match to S52's label: a paired with/without-tool outcome difference supervises the boundary. PARTIAL as token-level precedent: CoBRA's label is per trajectory/instance, while S52 broadcasts a prompt-level delta to token rows and predicts it from the pre-read hidden state

sources.topic: cost-aware gating and pre-execution utility prediction
sources.citation: Liang He, Jingbo Wen, Hongyu Gu, Hao Li, Haoyu Wang, Yixiong Chen, Kangning Cui, Xilu Wang. From Relevance to Execution Utility: Reward-Aware Dynamic Execution Gating for Skill-Based LLM Agents. arXiv:2608.09168v1.
claims: A plausible retrieved bundle does not guarantee that executing it is worthwhile, and every conditioned rollout is expensive.
RADEG predicts execution utility before the expensive rollout from a low-cost surrogate.
Matched same-query rollouts that perturb the bundle isolate composition effects for supervision.
Under a held-out evaluation it reduces unnecessary executions while preserving a large fraction of verifier reward.
sources.how_verified: abstract read on 2026-11-17 from the arXiv API record for 2608.09168
sources.relevance: direct support for a cost-aware pre-execution gate trained on matched rollouts; the utility is the verifier reward, as in S52's verified-outcome difference

sources.citation: Helia Hashemi, Victor Ruhle, Saravan Rajmohan. Cost-Aware Retrieval-Augmentation Reasoning Models with Adaptive Retrieval Depth. arXiv:2510.15719v1.
claims: Both retrieval and reasoning tokens contribute substantially to cost.
The paper develops a cost-aware advantage function for reinforcement learning of efficient retrieval-augmented reasoning.
Across seven QA datasets it reports roughly 16-20% lower latency and about +5% average exact match.
sources.how_verified: abstract read on 2026-11-17 from the arXiv API record for 2510.15719
sources.relevance: cost belongs in the objective rather than in a post-hoc filter; S52 keeps the cost in physical bytes and sweeps the threshold instead of pricing bytes in nats

sources.citation: Sanjay Mishra. Cost-Aware Query Routing in RAG: Empirical Analysis of Retrieval Depth Tradeoffs. arXiv:2606.02581v1.
claims: Static retrieval configurations cannot resolve the quality/cost/latency trade-off across heterogeneous queries.
CA-RAG routes each query to a strategy bundle, including retrieval-free direct inference, by maximizing a utility that combines a quality prior with latency and billed-token penalties.
It reports 26% fewer billed tokens than always-heavy retrieval and 34% lower mean latency than always-direct inference while maintaining equivalent answer quality.
sources.how_verified: abstract read on 2026-11-17 from the arXiv API record for 2606.02581
sources.relevance: published evidence that a pre-retrieval route can preserve quality at lower measured cost; it is query-level and the benchmark is 28 queries, so the quality equivalence is not a token-level routing result

sources.citation: Zhouting Zhao. When Is Additional Retrieval Worthwhile? A Cost-Aware Study of Evidence Gain and Answer Reliability in RAG. arXiv:2610.37358v1.
claims: The paper estimates the question-specific incremental evidence-retrieval benefit of a stronger retriever using features available before the routing decision.
The routing model and threshold are frozen before held-out evaluation, on document-grouped cross-validation.

On 188 held-out questions the policy triggers the stronger retriever on 24.5% and matches always-stronger evidence Hit@10, but paired bootstrap intervals do not establish a reliable utility advantage.

The author reports no clear correctness or faithfulness improvement in provisional answer-level assessment and labels the work a reproducible empirical study, not established answer-quality superiority.
sources.how_verified: abstract read on 2026-11-17 from the arXiv API record for 2610.37358
sources.relevance: the most directly relevant caution: a pre-decision benefit estimate can save retrieval without preserving answer quality. S52 therefore makes exact-answer accuracy and the matched controls part of the win bar, not read savings alone

sources.citation: Isaac Ong, Amjad Almahairi, Vincent Wu, Wei-Lin Chiang, Tianhao Wu, Joseph E. Gonzalez, M Waleed Kadous, Ion Stoica. RouteLLM: Learning to Route LLMs with Preference Data. arXiv:2406.18665v4.
claims: A router can choose between a stronger and a weaker model at inference to trade cost against quality.
Routers trained on preference data reduce cost by over 2x in some cases without compromising response quality.
Router models transfer when the strong and weak models change.
sources.relevance: cost-aware routing with preserved quality, but the routed action is which model answers, not whether to fetch memory before a token. It supports the shape of the win bar, not the S52 mechanism

sources.citation: Hanze Dong, Wei Xiong, Deepanshu Goyal, Yihan Zhang, Winnie Chow, Rui Pan, Shizhe Diao, Jipeng Zhang, Kashun Shum, Tong Zhang. RAFT: Reward rAnked FineTuning for Generative Foundation Model Alignment. TMLR. arXiv:2304.06767v4.
claims: A reward model plus a sufficient number of sampled responses can select high-quality samples and discard undesired ones.
Fine-tuning on the filtered samples improves the model under reward and other automated metrics.
sources.relevance: verifies rollout selection as supervision, but RAFT ranks a single condition's samples; it does not form a paired with/without-memory difference, so it does not establish the S52 label

sources.topic: counterfactual utility labels from paired rollouts
sources.citation: No primary source found that trains a per-token pre-read router on a paired with/without-memory verified-outcome difference and evaluates it with a mask-enforced sparse read.
claims: CoBRA and RADEG use paired with/without-tool or matched-bundle rollouts at the instance/trajectory level.
No paper found estimates a per-token utility label by pairing the same prompt's rollouts with and without an external memory read.
sources.how_verified: absence of evidence from the arXiv searches above; not evidence of absence
sources.relevance: this is the gap the S52 screen tests; the registration keeps the claim at the prompt-level label and does not assert token-level utility identification

conclusion.pre_fetch_routing: Pre-fetch retrieval decisions are well established (Adaptive-RAG, Self-RAG, FLARE, DRAGIN). Adaptive-RAG in particular trains its router on actual model outcomes, which is the closest precedent for outcome-supervised routing.
conclusion.counterfactual_labels: Paired with/without-tool rollouts are published (CoBRA, RADEG, TQG-Exp) but at instance or trajectory granularity. A per-token pre-read utility label is not published as far as these searches reach; S52 registers a prompt-level label and says so.
conclusion.cost_aware: Cost-aware routing is published and can preserve quality at lower billed cost (CA-RAG, cost-aware depth). The 2026 cost-aware evidence-gain study is the important counterweight: a pre-decision benefit estimate can save retrieval without improving answer correctness, so accuracy against base and a matched control is part of the S52 win bar.
conclusion.quality_preservation: Published evidence that routing before retrieval preserves quality is PARTIAL: strong at query level for Adaptive-RAG and CA-RAG; not established for token-level memory routing and explicitly not established for answer quality in arXiv:2610.37358.
